title: Twins with differences
caption: The spiral galaxy NGC 7331, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 7331 · constellation Pegasus · about 45 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Ranked #72 on ESA/Hubble’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: Arms swirl like a whirlpool around a bright central region in this Hubble view of NGC 7331, a spiral galaxy about 45 million light-years away in Pegasus, the Winged Horse, turned partly edge-on toward us. Near the yellow core, a tiny red dot marks a supernova that can still be faintly seen.

That supernova, SN2014C, is why the picture was taken. In just one year it changed from an explosion with very little hydrogen into one rich in hydrogen. This rarely seen transformation was bright at high energies and offers rare insight into the poorly understood final stages of massive stars.

In many ways NGC 7331 resembles the Milky Way: similar in size, shape and mass, with a comparable star formation rate, number of stars, central supermassive black hole and spiral arms. The main difference is that it has no bar of stars, gas and dust across its middle. Its central bulge also spins the opposite way to its disc.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.68 x 2.01 arcminutes) and distance (45 million light years), the frame spans roughly 35,000 × 26,000 light-years. Its light set out about 45 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 observed from ultraviolet through visible to near-infrared light, including a hydrogen-alpha filter; the colour mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: The ultraviolet and near-infrared parts of this light are invisible to the eye.

explore: William Herschel first spotted NGC 7331 in 1784. Studying galaxies like it is a way of holding up a mirror to our own, helping astronomers understand parts of the Milky Way we cannot easily observe, as well as how galaxies behave and evolve in general.
alt: A partly edge-on spiral galaxy with swirling arms around a yellow core, with a tiny red dot near the centre.
